name: OmniBot Academy & Workshop
tag: Hands-on courses with AI tutors you can talk to, from networking to auto repair and IoT.

scenarios.title: Learn home networking
scenarios.ask: I'm a {level} and can study {hours} a week for {weeks} weeks. Teach me networking.
steps: Placement
Asked 8 quick questions and skipped {=(level - 1) * 3} lessons you already know.
Tutor
Built a path of {=max(4, weeks * 2 - (level - 1) * 3)} lessons: IP addresses, subnets, DNS, Wi-Fi and troubleshooting.
Lab
Set up a virtual home network with {=weeks} labs, one per week, where you break and fix things safely.
Voice tutor
Ready to answer questions out loud while you work through each lab.

result.title: Course plan
rows: About {=round(hours * weeks / max(4, weeks * 2 - (level - 1) * 3), 1)} hours per lesson

followups: Does it lead to a certificate?
You get a course completion record. It prepares you for entry-level networking study, but it is not an industry certification.
Can I ask the tutor anything?
Yes, by voice or text. It stays on the course topic and points you to the right lesson.

scenarios.title: Teach a brake inspection class
scenarios.ask: Run a workshop for {students} students on inspecting disc brakes over {sessions} sessions.
steps: Tutor
Built lessons on pads, rotors, calipers and brake fluid, with 3D parts students can take apart.
Diagnostics coach
Walks through sounds and symptoms, such as squeal, grinding and a soft pedal, and what each usually points to.
Safety
Added a lift and jack safety check before every hands-on step.
Tracker
Logs each student's checklist so you see who is ready to work under supervision.
followups: Can students do real brake work after this?
They learn to inspect and explain what they see. Brakes are safety-critical, so repairs should be checked by a qualified mechanic.
Yes. The auto track also covers batteries, charging, cooling and basic engine diagnostics.

scenarios.title: Build an IoT soil sensor
scenarios.ask: Teach me to build {sensors} soil moisture sensor(s) that report to my phone, using the {kit}.
steps: Tutor
Explained how a soil probe, a small Wi-Fi board and a battery fit together.
Parts list
Built a parts list at about ${=kit} per sensor, plus a shared hub.
Code coach
Walked through the sensor code line by line and had you change the reading interval.
Dashboard
Connected {sensors} sensor(s) to a phone dashboard with a dry-soil alert.
followups: Do I need to know how to code?
No. The tutor explains each line and you only change a few values.
Reading once an hour, a typical sensor runs for weeks to months, depending on the battery and Wi-Fi signal.
